macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures rebound as oil retreats and investors weigh Iran tensions
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures edged higher after global markets steadied and oil prices eased following fresh U.S. strikes on Iran, which had revived geopolitical anxiety. The Reuters report also noted that European shares rose in choppy trading while Asian shares advanced, though gains were capped by oil-driven inflation fears.

items.title: Oil price shock remains the dominant macro driver
items.summary: Reuters reported that oil prices rose sharply after the U.S. launched fresh strikes against Iran, renewing fears of supply disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz and stoking inflation concerns. MarketScreener also noted oil was drifting down later after OPEC+ agreed to raise output targets.

items.title: Fed caution keeps risk appetite restrained in Asian trading
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that Australian shares wobbled as Federal Reserve caution tempered optimism from lower oil prices, highlighting ongoing sensitivity to central-bank rhetoric. Reuters separately said some Fed officials saw a need for future rate rises to contain inflation, reinforcing the hawkish policy backdrop.

items.title: Yen remains under pressure as Japan’s bond yields hit multi-decade highs
items.summary: Reuters said the U.S. dollar held firm while the Japanese yen stayed under pressure as higher oil prices revived rate-hike bets. It also reported that the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield hit a 30-year high amid renewed inflation worries and concerns about Japan’s fiscal health.

items.title: China inflation and producer prices underscore sticky cost pressures
items.summary: Reuters reported that China’s producer price inflation rose for a fourth straight month in June to its highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also extended gains. The data pointed to persistent upstream cost pressures for manufacturers.

items.title: India inflation likely exceeded the central bank’s 4% target
items.summary: A Reuters poll found India’s consumer inflation likely breached the Reserve Bank of India’s medium-term target for the first time in 16 months, driven by higher food and fuel prices, U.S.-Iran war-related energy pressures, and a weak monsoon. That would complicate the central bank’s policy outlook.

items.title: US earnings season continues with PepsiCo and other large-cap movers
items.summary: Yahoo Finance highlighted PepsiCo’s stronger-than-expected revenue in the second quarter despite weaker North American demand, signaling strain from cautious consumer spending. CNBC also flagged premarket moves in names including AstraZeneca, PepsiCo, Salesforce, and Levi Strauss.

items.title: Asian markets mixed as AI and chip stocks remain volatile
items.summary: AP reported that shares were mostly lower in Asia after another sell-off in artificial-intelligence stocks hit the U.S. market, though sentiment improved when a deal was announced to end the Iran war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. MarketScreener also noted Samsung Electronics was among the most-mentioned gainers, up 8.22% over 24 hours.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work to automate tasks across apps and files
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across different applications and files, intensifying competition in workplace AI tools. Reuters also reported broader OpenAI product changes around its desktop and voice offerings this week.

items.title: OpenAI broadly releases GPT-5.6 and expands model lineup
items.summary: Techmeme reports that OpenAI broadly released GPT-5.6 in multiple tiers, with pricing aimed at different performance levels. The launch also accompanied a push toward more capable professional workflows through ChatGPT Work.

items.title: Meta opens Muse Spark 1.1 to developers via public API preview
items.summary: Meta released Muse Spark 1.1 to U.S. developers in a public API preview, positioning it as a stronger coding-focused model than the first generation. The release adds more pressure in the race to monetize enterprise AI access.

items.title: Meta announces Meta Model API with aggressive pricing
items.summary: Meta introduced a Meta Model API and said its pricing will be significantly below major rivals, signaling a more aggressive push into commercial AI infrastructure. Reuters also reported the company is preparing broader AI-chip and data-center expansion.

items.title: Anthropic adds a beta reflection dashboard for Claude users
items.summary: Anthropic debuted a reflection dashboard in beta for Free, Pro, and Max users with memory enabled, giving users a way to review their Claude activity over time. The move reflects the company’s focus on personalization and user control in consumer AI.

items.title: xAI releases Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: Reuters reported that xAI launched Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model so far and optimized for coding and agent-like workflows. The release adds another major model update in the fast-moving foundation-model race.

items.title: Anthropic appoints Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic said it appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body designed to keep the company aligned with its public-interest mission. The move underscores growing governance scrutiny around frontier AI firms.

items.title: Meta plans to manufacture an AI chip starting in September
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to begin manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip in September as part of a broader effort to expand computing capacity. The company is also increasing data-center and infrastructure spending to support AI growth.

items.title: Micron announces more than $250 billion U.S. investment driven by AI demand
items.summary: Micron said it plans to invest more than $250 billion in the United States through 2035, citing surging demand for memory chips in the AI era. The announcement reflects how AI continues to reshape semiconductor capital spending.

items.title: China tightens its AI ecosystem as U.S. restrictions deepen
items.summary: Reuters reported that China is moving to build a more self-contained AI stack, including open-source models, as Washington expands limits on foreign access to top-tier AI technology. The trend highlights accelerating geopolitical fragmentation in AI.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony to end production of physical PlayStation game discs in January 2028
items.summary: Sony has reportedly clarified that new PlayStation games will be digital-only after January 2028, marking a major shift away from physical media. The change would affect all new PS5 titles and retail distribution going forward.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass growth falls short of Microsoft’s expectations
items.summary: IGN reports that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said Game Pass has not grown as Microsoft expected, with subscriber numbers reportedly tens of millions below previous targets. The admission highlights ongoing pressure on Xbox’s subscription strategy.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports released on PS4 and PS5
items.summary: IGN says both Black Ops 1 and Black Ops 2 are now available on PS4 and PS5. The release is notable for bringing older Call of Duty entries to modern PlayStation consoles, though at a premium price.

items.title: Pokémon GO marks its 10th anniversary with a livestream event
items.summary: IGN reports that Pokémon GO is celebrating its 10th anniversary with a special livestream. The event is expected to include announcements and surprises for players.

items.title: Nintendo to shut down Mario Kart Tour this September
items.summary: IGN says Nintendo will end service for Mario Kart Tour in September after seven years. The shutdown closes one of Nintendo’s longest-running mobile racing games.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced surges on Steam
items.summary: IGN reports that Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced reached around 100,000 concurrent players on Steam, the highest peak for any game in the franchise so far. The strong launch signals major interest in the resynced release.

items.title: Fortnite adds American Dad crossover bundle
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Epic Games released an American Dad crossover bundle in Fortnite’s Item Shop. Fans were disappointed that Roger was not included in the bundle.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 to get its own standalone launcher
items.summary: VGTimes says Black Ops 6 will become a separate title with its own dedicated launcher starting July 7. The game will no longer be accessed through the unified Call of Duty HQ hub.

items.title: Epic Games settles lawsuit tied to Fortnite leaks
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Epic Games has settled its lawsuit against former contractor Hayden Cohen, who was accused of leaking confidential information about upcoming Fortnite collaborations. The settlement closes a high-profile legal dispute for the company.

items.title: Minecraft investment reportedly increasing under Microsoft restructuring
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Microsoft plans to boost investment in Minecraft following an internal restructuring. Mojang will now reportedly report directly to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.
